items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: we had a great minister, Reverend Brown, and he loved classical music. And he started asking me to also play classical trumpet solos in church

ctx.x: Well let me take you back for a minute. The vocalizing in the church was your first kind of serious exposure to music. When did the trumpet come along?

Well the trumpet was there the whole time and I always listened to the trumpet, but in terms of you know you have more opportunities to sing in church than you do to play but actually what would happen is we had a great minister, Reverend Brown, and he loved classical music. And he started asking me to also play classical trumpet solos in church, which there’s nothing better. Every trumpet player on Easter can get a gig too, you know? Even guys that suck, it’s true. It’s funny, I played this Easter I played a…
A trumpet owner — I like that.
